alignments.note: Imperative rendered *hope*; no subject pronoun is written for it.
Vocative takes the supplied *O* into its own unit under rule 36.
Preposition takes the word the ASV wrote for its relation, *in*, under rule 11.
כִּי takes the *For* written for it under rule 14.

Verbless clause with a prepositional predicate: the construction-supplied copula and the presentative dummy *there* join the preposition under rules 20 and 49, headed on the preposition. Unit discontinuous around the name by rule 25.
Divine name as the preposition's object.
The ASV writes no *the* for הַחֶסֶד; the article is unrepresented under rule 29.
Subject noun keeps its own word.
Waw takes the *And* written for it under rule 14.
הַרְבֵּה is rendered by the single adjectival word *plenteous*, which is the whole of what the ASV spends on it.

Second prepositional predicate takes the construction-supplied copula under rules 20 and 49, headed on the preposition; unit discontinuous around the suffix's pronoun by rule 25. No dummy *there* is written in this colon.
Suffix takes the pronoun written for it under rule 18.
Subject noun keeps its own word.

review_notes: Both כִּי clauses are read as prepositional predicates with nominal subjects, so the copulas go to עִם under rule 49's closing paragraph; the competing reading would put *there is* on חֶסֶד and *is* on פְּדוּת.
הַרְבֵּה is read as an adverbial infinitive absolute whose whole contribution the ASV writes as *plenteous*, on the terms of rule 56.
